sources.title: Connected Nations 2025
sources.license: Ofcom terms / OGL for published data
sources.lines: main report index, methodology, interactive report and data downloads
facts: Connected Nations 2025 is Ofcom's annual report on broadband and mobile availability in the UK.
The report was published on 19 November 2025 and uses a July 2025 data vintage.
Ofcom publishes a UK report, separate nation reports, an interactive report and data downloads.
Coverage, performance and take-up are separate measures and must not be conflated.
Area-level reporting cannot be promoted to exact parcel service without address-level evidence.

sources.title: Nations report 2025
sources.lines: England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales summaries
facts: The Nations report page publishes separate broadband and mobile summaries for each UK nation.
For England it reports gigabit-capable coverage of 88% or 21.1 million residential premises at the July 2025 vintage.
It reports 79% full-fibre availability for residential premises in England.
Nation-level percentages and counts are aggregate statistics, not exact property observations.
Coverage outside premises, geographic coverage and indoor coverage must remain separate.

sources.title: Data downloads 2025
facts: The page provides downloadable datasets underpinning Connected Nations 2025.
Ofcom states the downloads support year-on-year comparisons of communications infrastructure.
Each file's geography, unit, vintage and field definitions must be retained.
Download availability does not mean every dataset is address-level or suitable for parcel promotion.
Exact service claims require a compatible premises identifier and current orderability evidence.

sources.title: Connected Nations 2025 Methodology Annex
sources.lines: P3-P7 premise base, matching and fixed coverage methodology
facts: Ofcom used AddressBase Premium and Islands Epoch 119 to construct the July 2025 premise base.
The methodology received more than 124 million fixed-broadband availability records.
Almost all uniquely identified premises, 99.7%, matched at least one provider record using UPRN or building address.
Providers were asked for premises where an end-user could order service with a 1 July 2025 reference date.
Ofcom excluded postcode-only estimates from address-level coverage analysis to preserve accuracy.

sources.title: About this data — fixed broadband performance
sources.lines: P1-P2 file scope, fields and comparison notes
facts: Fifty-seven fixed broadband providers submitted active-line information for the July 2025 snapshot.
The dataset covers active residential and business connections, technologies and upload or download speeds.
Ofcom publishes four geographic levels: local authority, Westminster constituency, devolved constituency and census output area.
Since 2024 Ofcom uses maximum speeds and no longer reports performance at postcode level.
Performance of active lines is distinct from network availability and exact parcel orderability.

sources.title: Connected Nations 2025 England Report
sources.lines: P6 broadband and P13-P15 mobile coverage
facts: The England report uses provider and mobile-operator data with a July 2025 reference date.
It reports gigabit-capable broadband availability of 92% for urban premises and 61% for rural premises in England.
England 5G standalone coverage outside premises is reported at 85% high confidence and 75% very high confidence.
Coverage outside premises is a prediction for the 100 by 100 metre area containing a dwelling.
Nation and area statistics cannot be promoted to an exact address-level current service statement.

sources.title: Connected Nations update: Spring 2025
facts: The Spring 2025 update provides a January 2025 snapshot of mobile coverage and fixed broadband availability.
It is an interim update to Connected Nations 2024.
Ofcom states that wide-area mobile reporting has limitations for assessing coverage at a particular location.
The January 2025 vintage must remain distinct from July 2025 and January 2026 releases.
Predicted mobile coverage is not sufficient evidence of service at a specific parcel.

sources.title: Project Gigabit network build contract — Cheshire
sources.lines: termination and February 2026 call-off eight update
facts: BDUK and Freedom Fibre mutually agreed to terminate the original Cheshire contract.
BDUK states Freedom Fibre received no public funding for that contract.
In February 2026 BDUK added Cheshire premises to Openreach call-off eight.
Call-off eight was valued at £37.5 million and targeted around 18,500 hard-to-reach premises.
Contract award or replacement status does not prove a live retail service at each premise.

sources.title: Project Gigabit network build contract — Mid West Shropshire
facts: In October 2025 BDUK agreed a contract change covering Mid West Shropshire.
The premises were included within Openreach call-off three.
The guidance records a contract-scope change rather than completed delivery.
Contract scope and effective date must be retained in lineage.
Planned inclusion cannot be promoted to current parcel service without build and orderability evidence.

sources.title: Project Gigabit network build contract — Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire
facts: BDUK and CityFibre mutually agreed to end the Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire contract.
The May 2026 update attributes the change to market conditions and expanded commercial rollout.
The page says less public funding is required and the prior contract is no longer appropriate.
Terminated contract status must not remain represented as active planned delivery.
Alternative-supplier discussions are not proof of a live service at remaining premises.

sources.title: Project Gigabit framework agreement — Openreach
facts: The cross-regional framework was signed to deliver gigabit-capable broadband to hard-to-reach premises in Great Britain.
The page lists call-off contracts and records Cheshire as call-off eight signed in February 2026.
BDUK notes that premises counts can change following market research or engineering constraints.
Planning and build work must occur before residents can request a service.
Framework or call-off membership is not exact current retail orderability.

sources.title: Project Gigabit contracts
facts: The collection indexes Project Gigabit local, regional and framework contract guidance.
It includes active, redesigned, transferred and terminated contract pages.
Contract status must be resolved from each current guidance page rather than assumed from the collection title.
Area and contract entries are administrative delivery context.
Parcel service promotion remains blocked without exact identity, completed build and current orderability.

sources.title: Building Digital UK annual report and accounts 2022 to 2023
facts: The document is BDUK's corporate annual report and accounts for 2022 to 2023.
It describes the transition of gigabit contracts from procurement toward contract delivery management.
Corporate reporting supplies programme context rather than current coverage observations.
Historic financial-year statements require explicit reporting-period lineage.
Corporate programme status cannot be promoted to exact present-day parcel service.
